messages:
maria: Heads-up — canary p95 decode latency jumped ~40% after merge of runtime PR #4123 (fused-op-selector + batch heuristics). CI perf job perf-ci/runtime/decode-path failed.

alex: Seen it. Reproducer on a 4k token streaming workload — latency spikes when KV cache size hits eviction threshold.

tim: Quick flamegraph from canary (annotated):
```
decode_kernel > fused_attention > kv_cache_miss_handler > recompute_attn
```

maria: CI link: https://ci.redwood.ai/jobs/98765/artifacts (perf diffs attached)

ci-bot: perf-ci/runtime/decode-path: failed — p95 latency +42% vs baseline. (build 98765)

alex: Bisect points to commit 8f3bd9e (PR #4123) — the fused-op-selector changed ordering and added aggressive batch coalescing, which increases prefix queueing and causes premature KV eviction under skewed seqlen.

dalia: I can whip up a minimal repro script. Try:
```
python tools/perf/repro.py --model redwood/v1 --seq-len 4096 --batching coalesce --kv-cap 3
```

maria: Can we hold the rollout? If it's the PR we should revert and then reintroduce with a safety check.

infra-bot: Deployments to canary paused by maria.rolling-hold (reason: perf regression). :pause_button:

laura: Revert PR #4123 landed (8f3bd9e reverted). Canary p95 returned to baseline in 20m. Need follow-up: make fused-op-selector aware of kv occupancy and avoid coalescing across hot prefixes.

alex: I'll open follow-up issue + patch. Short-term: tweak batcher config to limit coalesce window. Filed: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/RW-7891

maria: Thanks — closing the incident after postmortem. Add perf test that simulates long-prefix KV churn.
